idea: How to prevent bathroom pipe problems
title: Preventing Bathroom Drain Clogs at the P-Trap
description: An educational breakdown showing how hair and soap scum collect inside a bathroom P-trap, demonstrating why mechanical prevention and manual trap maintenance are superior to aggressive chemical treatments.
image_prompt: Vertical 9:16 photorealistic educational cutaway section beneath a residential bathroom sink vanity. The image shows a realistic cross-section view of standard white PVC drain piping: a chrome drain assembly in the sink basin, leading down through a smooth vertical tailpiece into a curved P-trap fitting, which connects to a horizontal waste pipe entering the wall. Inside the curved trap water seal, a clear physical build-up of hair strands and soap residue is shown contained within the dip of the trap. Bright, clean natural lighting inside a realistic cabinet interior. Centered composition with clean visual space in the top third and bottom third. No text, no arrows, no labels, no logos, no watermarks, photorealistic detail, physically realistic plumbing connections.
visual_story: The viewer observes a detailed cutaway of the drain system under a bathroom vanity. The visual highlights the standard P-trap section where water rests to seal sewer gases, showing how hair and organic debris naturally gather in the trap loop before reaching the main branch drain. This visual establishes that most bathroom blockages are accessible and preventable at the fixture level.

on_image_text.hook: Stop Bathroom Clogs Before They Reach Your Wall
on_image_text.explanation: Hair and soap scum settle inside the P-trap dip before reaching the main branch drain.
on_image_text.takeaway: Use surface strainers and clean the P-trap manually to protect downstream piping.
